_readme: REVIEWED subtopic assignment for the Mathematical Logic board PYQs.
Assigned by reading each stem against the chapter's EXISTING axis — the 266
textbook practice rows already filed there — not against the compilation's own
A./B./C. section letters, which are a coarser and different cut. Sampled the
live rows per subtopic on 2026-08-13 before assigning; two calls turn on what
- The bare pattern [(p->q) ^ q] -> p is filed under TRUTH TABLES, while the
'examine whether it is a tautology / contradiction' phrasing of the SAME
pattern is filed under TAUTOLOGY, CONTRADICTION AND CONTINGENCY. So #19
('Construct the truth table for ...') and #13 ('Examine whether ...') carry
the same statement pattern and land on different subtopics. That is the
bank's existing convention, and it is right: the ASK is what differs.
- Anything written as an equivalence (=) goes to LOGICAL EQUIVALENCE AND
ALGEBRA OF STATEMENTS whether or not it is proved with a truth table, so
#15/#16/#17/#20 (with a table) and #18 ('without using truth table') all sit
'Truth values of a compound statement' (#2, #4) goes to STATEMENTS AND LOGICAL
CONNECTIVES, matching rows like 'The square of any even number is odd or the
cube of any odd number is odd' already filed there.
